question: to the Commission Arkadiusz Mularczyk (ECR) Subject:

According to press coverage and reports from the Comité International de Mauthausen (International Mauthausen Committee -– CIM), commercial development is under way on the site of a former subcamp of the Mauthausen concentration camp complex in Leobersdorf, Austria, where a supermarket and a logistics centre are being built. Between 1944 and 1945, around 400 women and girls were imprisoned there and forced into slave labour; many of them subsequently perished during the death march to Mauthausen. The CIM stresses that the traces of these crimes are being destroyed and buried under layers of gravel, steel and concrete. The Mauthausen concentration camp complex held around 190 000 prisoners, of whom almost 90 000 perished1. In response to Question P-002018/20242, the Commission stated that ‘[t]he Commission has supported the Member States to maintain memorial sites of former Nazi concentration and death camps through EU funds’ and that the Commission ‘will continue to do so’. The commercial development of a site where victims suffered stands in blatant contradiction to this commitment and to the EU’s policy on European remembrance. Within the framework of its powers under Article 167 TFEU, what specific measures is the Commission taking, or does it intend to take, to encourage the Member State (Austria) to protect this memorial site from commercial development?
